segments.narration: The message says: resurrect dead on planet Jupiter. It is glued into the street.
Hundreds of these tiles have surfaced since the first one in Philadelphia in 1983, across roughly two dozen American cities and three in South America.
Each is layered linoleum and asphalt crack filler, about twelve inches by six, laid on hot tar and left for traffic to press flat.
So how do you tile a busy intersection with nobody ever seeing you do it? A 2011 documentary followed the trail to a reclusive Philadelphian named Severino Verna.
Their answer: he cut a hole in the floor of his car and lowered each tile through it while driving. Neighbours had noticed the missing passenger seat. Verna never confirmed a word of it.
